utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to ask you the same questions again today, would your answers be essentially the same as in the statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They would be essentially the same.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this statement given under Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3690, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now read out a brief summary of Mr. Nedjo Nikolic's statement. [In English] Mr. Nedjo Nikolic was the director of the Ciglane brick factory in Bratunac during July 1995. Mr. Nikolic recalls that on the morning of 14th of July, 1995, five or six men in uniform came to his office and asked whether some Muslims from Srebrenica could be put up temporarily on the grounds of the factory. Mr. Nikolic showed the men around the factory grounds, and particularly the open area of the factory. One of the men, Colonel Beara, asked if Mr. Nikolic could provide drinking water for the prisoners. Mr. Nikolic said that they could do that. However, after receiving a telephone call, Colonel Beara and the men seemed disinterested in using the brick factory and left. Mr. Nikolic never heard from them again. Mr. Nedjo Nikolic refutes Prosecution Witness Momir Nikolic's testimony that Momir Nikolic did not come to the brick factory on the morning of 14 July, 1995. Nedjo Nikolic is positive that Momir Nikolic was one of the persons who came to the brick factory with Colonel Beara on the morning of 14th of July. Nedjo Nikolic had known Momir Nikolic for about 20 years at that time. Mr. Nedjo Nikolic also refutes the testimony of Momir Nikolic that there was a plan from 12th of July, 1995, to take the Muslim prisoners from Srebrenica to the brick factory to be executed. No one had come and asked about using the brickworks for prisoners prior to the visit of the group on the morning of 14th of July, 1995. The brick factory premises were unsuitable as a place to execute prisoners because there were about 50 employees at the factory at that time and there were people living nearby. Nedjo Nikolic also refutes the testimony of Momir Nikolic that the officers who came to the brick factory asked the director about this place as a possible execution site. During the visit on 14th of July, 1995, no one made any reference to an execution site or to killings. And that is the summary. I do not have questions for Mr. Nikolic at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, as you have noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in its entirety in writing, that is, through your written witness statement. And now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, good morning. Now, at paragraph 4 of your statement you said that you were a member of the SDS since its founding. Now, you were also a candidate for the SDS at the Bratunac Municipal Assembly election in 1990; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I have been an SDS member since its foundation and I was a candidate as well as a member of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac from 1990 till 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you also said that you were a member of the SDS Municipal Board, and if I'm not wrong you were a member of that board from July 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, not July 1991. From 1990, since the foundation of the Serb Democratic Party, until 1998, that's when I was a member of the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were also a member - you may have mentioned it already - of the Serbian Municipal Assembly when it first was established in 1991, right, so not just the party but also the Serb institution in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac from 1990 when the first multi-party elections were held until the war. It was not a Serbian municipality. It was the municipality of Bratunac where there were also other ethnicities such as Muslims and Croats. The Municipal Assembly did not operate from the beginning till the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You are -- you know Jovan Nikolic, he's your cousin, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know Jovan Nikolic, he is a relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And he was the manager of the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was the manager of the co-operative in Kravica. It was called Zadruga. That's -- it -- the facilities, the buildings, belonged to Zadruga.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And in July 1995 you both lived in Bratunac in Gavrila Principa Street, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you were living in the same building; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The same building, the same storey, our apartments were next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, in your statement at paragraph 14 you explained that you were mobilised between the 10th and the 13th of July, and that on the 13th of July you resumed your work; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I came from the front line on the 13th and on the 14th I reported at the company to continue working. So it was on the 14th, not the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So what it says on paragraph 14 of the statement is inaccurate because it says, and I read: "On 13 July we were back at our enterprises and resumed our work. In the evening of the same day, I came to Bratunac and went straight to my flat, had a bath, and I went to sleep." So you're talking about the 13th of July in your statement. Are you now saying that it was the 14th?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please, I came from the front line, that is, I was demobilised on the 13th and went home to rest because I had been away for three or four days. And on the following day, the 14th, I went to work. That's what I said and that's what it says or it should.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, that's not what the -- that's not what your statement says because your statement says that on the 13th you were back at our enterprise and resumed our work. So now you specified and you explained that what you meant here to say was that on the 13th you went back home and then the day after you went back to the brick factory. Is this your testimony now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- upload his statement. Exhibit 3690.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And it's page 4 of the English translation and page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So can you read your statement --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This is what I said. On the 13th of July, 1995, we were returned to our companies to continue working, which means that we were released from the front lines. I -- on the evening of that day, I came to Bratunac, I went to my flat, had a bath, and went to bed because the previous nights I did not sleep. That was on the 13th. On that day I did not go to my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you also said at paragraph 19 that in these days, meaning 13 and 14 I understand, you didn't notice anything particular happening in town, anything particular happening, because, and I quote, you were going from your flat directly to work and back. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, on 21st February 2012 you testified before the BiH state court as a defence witness in the case against Dragan Neskovic and Zoran Ilic; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: You didn't testify?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. Zoran Neskovic, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 25208.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the first and the second paragraph, it said that: [As read] "Nedjo Nikolic, former members of the Army of Republika Srpska Bratunac Brigade 3rd Battalion and defence witness of ... Ilic said that on the 13th and 14th of July they saw Ilic in Bratunac." And then further down there is a quotation from what appears to be your testimony that said: [As read] "'I went to the send-off party at the house of Jovan Ilic, Zoran's father, on the 13th of July ...'" So you're saying that this is not you, this is not your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I'm Nedjo Nikolic, son of Petar, from Kravica, and in the Bratunac municipality there are five men by the name of Nedjo Nikolic. I was never at that send-off party and I did not testify in the trial of Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. So on the night of the 13th you were back at home you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now can we have 65 ter 25223.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you will see this Chamber has been in Bratunac and is familiar with those places, but this is an aerial picture of the city. Now, if you look at this picture, Gavrila Principa is the street that leads to Konjevic Polje, so is the one in this picture that starts from the bottom and goes all the way up to the Hotel Fontana; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. On this -- I still haven't found it on this map, but Gavrila Principa Street runs to Fontana from the direction of Kravica or stretches that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if you can find the street, it is -- you see on the bottom it says "Konjevic Polje" with a red arrow and you see that just close by that label you see a street and it goes all the way up and then you see Hotel Fontana almost in the middle of the picture. Do you see that street now? Now, can you also locate your apartment building?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I've found it. Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Is it that big apartment building block on the left side of the street across to the road that leads to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters; correct? If we can ...

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's on the left turn. It's always the opposite direction from the building of the Bratunac Brigade and it's the third building on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: If we can zoom in a little bit around -- yeah. A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So it's this big apartment building block that we can see on the left side of the road; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's a series of buildings on the left side of this street. They are connected but autonomous. I'm in the third building on the left or when you enter the street it's on your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: If you could zoom in a little bit so for the benefit of everyone and the Chamber, is this -- yeah, a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And it's the big block that we see on the top of the picture now?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, if you can zoom out a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, the brick factory is in the direction of Ljubovija; correct? You can zoom all out.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So basically it is the street that you can see in this picture at the top of the image where there is an arrow that says "Ljubovija, Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. So to go from the brick factory to your apartment and vice versa, you drive across the town; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber has heard several testimony of the presence of many buses detaining thousands of Muslims, kept in buses in these and -- in this street and other locations, and some of them were precisely on your way home. So Zlatan Celanovic, for example, a member of the Bratunac Brigade, testified that the buses filled up a large portion of the street that connects the Vuk Karadzic school with the Gavrila Principa Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: If we can have P00257, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you will see the next picture is basically the same picture where the witness Celanovic marked the buses that he saw. What he said in his testimony, and it is page 27 of P0037, he said the vehicles were parked with an interval of 2 or 3 metres in the street. So there was a column of vehicles with 2 or 3 metres between them. They filled up the street, so every 2 or 3 metres there would be a parked vehicles and then again 2 or 3 metres and then again another parked vehicle, all the way up to the end of the street in front of the school. And if we can zoom in more or less at the centre of the picture where we can see there's a green mark. I think the picture is -- we should turn the picture exactly. Yeah, here we are. You will see that the street that leads to Gavrila Principa is where the witness marked all the buses. So are you saying that you never noticed anything on your way home on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When I arrived on the 13th of July, I didn't even go there. I went to the left immediately, to the building where I lived. I didn't go there and I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: You didn't go there, but you passed through, right, you --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you were -- you must have driven through Gavrila Principa Street, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Through Gavrila Principa Street to the apartment but not further than that, and further on is this building where the buses were and the street where the buses where.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But you were coming, if we look at this picture, from the up side of the road, from the Hotel Fontana directions because you were coming from the brick factory. So you passed by that street, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went to Ciglane only on the 14th in the morning at 7.00. Also, I did not want to take that street. I went straight to the intersection where the traffic lights are now and then to left towards Ljubovija, or rather --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I went apart from this street. I did not have any contact with that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. So when you got to your apartment, you must have seen or heard -- I mean, seen buses parked close to the stadium and heard shooting that night, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I really did not hear anything. I arrived tired and I went to bed straight away. My apartment is so good, it has such good isolation, that I did not hear anything, buses, shooting, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Nothing. So you were in Bratunac on the 13th evening, all this was happening behind the corner, and you haven't heard or seen nothing; this is your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's not exactly round the corner. It's certainly about 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Which is not very far you might agree. Now --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: All right. It's not far away but it's between that school that you're speaking of and my building -- I mean, there are quite a few buildings there, so if there were sound signals, I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But there are no buildings between your apartment and the stadium, as we can see from this picture? There is an empty field.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, not between the stadium and the building, but I don't know about the stadium, that anything was happening there. I haven't heard of anything happening at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, if we look at this evidence, this picture, you see that the witness marked three buses -- a series of buses also close to the stadium, you see that other little three crosses, these are other buses that could have been seen from the building.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, they could be seen, but I wasn't really watching anything and I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you didn't see anything, you didn't watch anything, you didn't hear anything. Yet, at paragraph 21 of your statement you show no doubt and you said that: "What happened in Bratunac," and you're referring to mistreatment, killings, and detention of Muslims, "has been spontaneous, not planned." Now, if you haven't heard, seen -- I mean, what is -- you don't have any basis for this assertion, do you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot claim anything that I had not seen and I had not seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So what I'm saying is that you can't even claim that it was spontaneous and not planned, the detention, transportation, killings of Muslims in Bratunac on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, was it spontaneous? I think it was spontaneous. It happened. Now, whether some plan had been made earlier on, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well. So you don't know. So what is at paragraph 21 is not correct. Now, the transportation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to answer the question? Do you agree with Prosecution's comment that your statement which said what happened in Bratunac had been spontaneous, not planned, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I claim yet again that all of that which happened was spontaneous, that there had not been a plan that planned for all of this to happen. Everything happened spontaneously and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was while you did not know anything, how did you know that it was spontaneous?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are my assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- then that answers the question. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you know Ziv -- sorry, Srbislav Davidovic, the president of Bratunac municipality Executive Board in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know the former president Srbislav Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yeah, my pronunciation wasn't impeccable. Now, he testified before this Chamber that on the 14th of July in the morning he met with Beara and two other officers at the Bratunac SDS office. Now, these other officers asked him to provide them with construction machineries. Davidovic then testified that he agreed to their request and called you to inform you that the military will come to take the loader at the brick factory. And this is Davidovic testimony is P04100 at pages 53, 54, 92, and 93. So my question for you is: Davidovic called you that morning and asked you, the morning of the 14th, and asked you to provide the military with the loader that you had at the brick factory; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is true that he called me and he said that the army would come and that they would ask for an excavator. That's a special machine, not a loader.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well, an excavator. And you did provide that machine to the army; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Later on, I don't know whether it was on that day or the following day, men from the military police came and they asked for that machine and I secured that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And that machine was actually used for the burial in mass graves of those killed at the Kravica warehouse; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I assume so, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you knew that you were giving your support to the burial operation of those executed down there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, before that they asked for machines too and they were mainly used for sanitisation of the terrain. I knew that they were going then, but that is natural in war time, to use machines, and I knew that there were casualties and I knew that the machine would be used for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But what is not natural is that a thousand people -- around a thousand people were killed and executed at the Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July, the day before, is it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not know that a thousand people were killed in Kravica on that day, and now whether 1.000 were killed at all, well that's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So let me ask you here because in fact in your statement you said something about Kravica and you said that you heard later that Muslims were killed. When did you actually learn about the event in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I heard perhaps on that day, the 14th in the afternoon, or the following day. I'm not sure exactly. But you know what? This information does not spread that quickly -- well, it's sort of hushed up and it's not that this information was accessible, so I couldn't hear about it very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, that's not what other witnesses have testified in this case, but you heard of it on the 13th -- on the 14th or the 15th, you said. And you probably discussed it with your cousin when you were back in the apartment; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Because he was informed of the killing already on the 13th in the evening. Did he tell you something that night when you went back?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: These were difficult days. I did not see my relative at all. His brother was killed on the following day, so we did not even talk. Up until then I didn't see him at all, so I couldn't have heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you described in your statement the killing. You said: "The Muslims who were being taken to the warehouse rebelled, seized the rifle from one of the soldiers or policemen, and killed him, and then started shooting at other guards." And then you said, same paragraph, paragraph 20: "The guards then panicked and in fear opened fire at the Muslims and killed a number of them." Now, I'm asking you today you know, don't you, that many Muslims were executed that day and that they were systematically and deliberately killed. It wasn't an action out of panic or fear; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please, I said there what it was that I heard. I was not an eye-witness and I cannot claim anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not asking you what you heard at the time. I'm asking you what you know now. What do you know now about Kravica? What do you know that happened in Kravica now?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that there were killings, that's evident, that there had been killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you agree that they were not in fear or in panic but there was a systematic and deliberate execution; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot claim that. How can I claim that, how that happened? This is what people were saying and now you claim that it's different. How can I tell? I'm not a court myself. I told you what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So if you were to tell the story to someone, you would still say that what happened in Kravica is that the guards panicked and in fear opened fire and killed a number of Muslims? This is the way you think things went?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that both happened. It is true that there were Muslim attacks, that a group grabbed a soldier's rifle and that there was shooting, that is true, and also it is true that there were killings. So I cannot claim either one or the other. I said what it was that I had heard.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that there were casualties on the Serb side and that is not reflected in the transcript. Line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, so you said that at that time it was normal to provide the excavator or the loader for sanitisation. Now my question for you is about the reburial operation. Now, you know, don't you, that around September or October 1995 the Bratunac civilian authorities together with the Bratunac Brigade exhumed and moved thousand of bodies from primary to secondary graves, including from Glogova, the one where your machinery were used; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I heard that. There had been some movement. I don't know whether my machines went then, maybe they did. I do not know, but I know that there were removals --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot follow both the witness and Mr. Karadzic at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, you interrupted the interpretation. Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Nikolic. You heard that, what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that there were movements, that there were removals of graves in 1995, but whether my machines went then I really don't know, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes? So we can continue, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wanted to ask the Prosecutor to tell us -- to give us a reference. How come it was the civilian authorities of Bratunac that did that? It would be a good thing if we knew about that if there are documents to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, you don't know with whether your machinery were involved. Well, let me refresh your memory and P140 who is a protected witness who testified in the Blagojevic case, he was the man who was operating the excavator or the loader during both the burial operation in Glogova and the reburial operation from Glogova. And what he testified in the Blagojevic case is that the same team was called back, meaning the same team who dug the graves in Glogova, the same team with the lorries and the machines, and this is transcript page 3435 and 3436 on the 23rd of October in the Blagojevic case. And again, when he's asked the following question: "Q. Can you describe the machine you were using to lift the bodies out of the graves? "A. Yes, I can. I can describe the machine. It's very much like the one in your sketch except that this type is a 160-B or C which doesn't make really any difference. It is a loader belonging to the brick works." Now, the same witness said that there was a yellow truck from the brick factory used both -- during both operations. So machines from the brick factory were, in fact, used also for the reburial operation in September and October. Would you agree with that? Do you remember this now?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I do not remember. However, if a man who operated this machine made this statement, then it is correct. I've forgotten, but I know that our machines were involved during that year, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you said you'd forgotten, but there are a few aspects that strike me as to why you have forgotten. The first question is: Wasn't it unusual to have a request of a loader and a truck month after the military operation in the area were finished? Didn't it strike you as peculiar?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I've already said a moment ago that the army often addressed us, asking us for some help in terms of sanitisation of the ground for burials and so on, and I did not find anything unusual in that. When I heard about relocations -- but even if I knew that it was something unusual, I couldn't do anything. When the army addresses us asking for a machine to be given to them, we just had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting you could have prevented or you could have said no, maybe you couldn't. But what I'm saying is that this is what you did and you should remember what happened. And there is another detail -- well, ...

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying even now, I mean, I cannot remember that detail, but I claim that if the man gave a statement, that that's what he did, then that is correct. But again, I cannot recall when that was done, I don't know the date or anything. That's why I said it's possible, but I don't remember. It is possible, I am saying that now. But now I'm saying again if the man who operated that machine said that, then that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, the same witness also said that when they returned the machine after the reburial operation, he said, and it's transcript page 3440 in the Blagojevic case: "The machine had been washed from the smell of the dead bodies because the stench had penetrated the cabin and all other parts of the machine." You don't recall that they brought back this machine after digging up bodies, carrying it somewhere else, and they had to be cleaned because they were stinking and you couldn't use them for the stench?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The machine was returned after the job was completed. Of course I remember that it was brought back. I would have remembered if it hadn't returned. But when a machine is returned after a few days, then that is the usual process. I remember that the machine was returned, of course I remember. As for the washing, I don't know about that. I did not wash it and I was not there in the machine to have felt the stench --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the last sentence because the interpreters couldn't follow you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As for the washing, I did not know about the washing. I didn't know that it was supposed to be washed because I'm not a machine operator. It's the machine operator who assessed that it should be washed and that's what he did. I, as director, did not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So let me move to another topic. Now, in your statement at paragraphs 15 and 18 you said that Beara, Branimir Tesic, Momir Nikolic, and a group of officers came to the brick factory on the morning of the 14th. Now, you said that at one point a telephone rang and it was a call for Mr. Beara; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And you also said that Beara took the phone and when the conversation finished he told the others that they were leaving. And that nobody --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: -- told --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He did not tell me anything. After the telephone conversation, he got up two or three minutes later and set out. He did not tell me anything, Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So -- and you said -- well, only Beara, so someone else told you something about the telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When leaving my office in the hall, Momir Nikolic just sort of discreetly whispered to me or told me softly that this combination was off; however, I did not say that in my statement. He said that to me discreetly, very softly, so that it could not be heard, and I thought that that was unimportant and I didn't mention it in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly the point that I wanted to get because on the 2nd of April, 2004, you gave a statement to the Blagojevic Defence; right? Now, in that statement which is 65 ter 25220, you didn't mention any call and you said: "In the meantime, one of the military officers, I think it was Momir Nikolic, arrived and said that this location had been given up and that the Muslim prisoners would not be held there. This was a final definitive order from above. I noticed that Beara became angry and when he heard this -- when he heard this, but he obviously had to accept it. After this announcement, they sat for a little longer and said good-bye and left." So now you changed a little bit what you said in your statement which get closer to what you said in 2004. But you see the inconsistency, don't you? Did you receive a telephone call for Beara or you didn't?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In my statement from 2004, I did mention the telephone conversation; however, these people who worked on the Defence team of Major Blagojevic did not record that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But you signed it, you signed the statement where you said that Momir Nikolic arrived and brought the news, to which Beara reacted. So why did you sign it if it's a different story?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I signed that. I believed that the Defence team left that out on purpose or that they wanted to leave it out, and I didn't want to oppose this wording. Momir did not say that publicly --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Should we just --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: -- he whispered to me --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you believe that the Defence team left it out and you didn't want -- and they didn't want this wording so you didn't say it publicly, so it sounds like you said you signed it because the Defence wanted you to sign it; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please, this is what I claim. The telephone conversation did take place --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: -- and I mentioned it. The Defence did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: -- I'm asking you something different now. I'm asking you whether it is true what you just said, which is true, having you said it, but that you left it out because you believed that the Defence team wanted that passage to be out. So you basically changed your version because you believed that the Defence in the Blagojevic case wanted you to say something different; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is correct, but I thought that this telephone conversation didn't really matter that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And let me ask you this question: Is there anything in the statement in this case that you provided to the Defence in the Karadzic that you changed because you thought that it was irrelevant or you changed because you thought that the Defence didn't want it to be there? Like, for example, that on the 14th you were informed of the Kravica warehouse massacres as you said a few minutes ago, whereas in the statement you said much later, if I'm not wrong. Let me go back to the statement, is there anything in the statement you have omitted because you thought the Defence didn't want to hear it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please, I was not there on the 14th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat. The interpreter did not hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, please repeat your answer. Could you start over again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I did not provide a statement. I did not say that I was informed on the 14th of any massacre in Kravica. I did not know that on the 14th. As for the statement I signed where there is no mention of the telephone conversation, I signed it because I believed the telephone conversation to be unimportant and that it didn't change anything. Also, I believed that it did not have any bearing on the essence, the gist, of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: You said something completely different to the Blagojevic Defence. You said that Momir came and informed you all about the new plan and the order coming from above. Now, this is something different and it's not just an irrelevant detail. Your story is different.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is not correct that Momir informed us all of some other plan. He only told me in the hallway that the plan was being scrapped. He was accompanied by Colonel Beara. He didn't dare comment anything, and I talked only to Beara. Momir was simply there close by in the hallway or in a nearby office. He didn't tell everyone that the plan was to be scrapped. He didn't dare nor could he say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Did he also tell you that the plan has changed because there was a final definitive order from above?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He told me, orders, there's a change to plan, that's all, and that's how I understood it, that the order came from above.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And Beara got upset?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Beara did not comment. It was my conclusion that he was upset. He got up, said nothing, and left. So it was my conclusion that there was a change to the plan and I concluded that he was upset. He no longer addressed me, got up, and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: You didn't conclude there was a change of plan; you were told there was a change of plan pursuant to an order from above. And then you may have concluded by looking at Beara that he was upset; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please, first, Beara got up and left, and on his way out Momir told me there was a change to plan, that is to say, after the telephone conversation. He told me that discreetly so that only I could hear. He didn't dare say it out loud. Beara was the person in charge of the process and of the talk with me. Momir could not answer any questions. He couldn't say that there was a change to plan. He was a junior officer there who couldn't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And Beara left without telling you anything? He stood up after the call and left?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, in December 2012 you gave another statement to this Defence, to the Karadzic Defence, a very short one which is 65 ter 1D05107. I'm not sure we need it, but in this statement you said something again slightly different. Instead of saying that you reached a conclusion that you weren't told nothing and now that Momir said something. You said that: "After the telephone conversation, Beara told me that he is giving up on Ciglane ..." So contrary to what you just said, Beara actually talked to you after the telephone conversation and told you that they were not bringing prisoners there anymore or whatever. What did he tell you after the telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Again, I repeat that Beara told me nothing after the telephone conversation. I never said he said anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So what you said -- let me check. If what you said to this Defence in December 2012 is then false because you said -- and I read it to you and you can see it on your screen. You said: "While we were sitting at the office someone called Beara by phone. And after the telephone conversation, Beara told me that he is giving up on 'Ciglane,' so no one of the Srebrenica Muslims was brought to 'Ciglane' where I was a manager." Can you see that? So that statement is also wrong?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Exactly. There is a mistake here. I don't know how it happened but he really said nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: In LiveNote page 71, line 2, it should be: I never said he ever said anything to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a mistake. There is a mistake in this part. He didn't say to me that they were giving up on Ciglane, it is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI

However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you and as a consequence you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question. But in that situation the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony compelled in such circumstances would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence save and except the offence of giving false testimony.
